title: Constructing simple geometrical figures
summary: Plan and verify constructions using rulers, compasses, set squares and protractors.
objectives: Choose suitable instruments and data for a geometric construction.
Construct and verify angle bisectors, perpendicular bisectors and parallel lines.
Construct triangles from SSS, SAS or ASA data and check that the data determine the figure.

blocks.text: SSS uses three side lengths, SAS uses two sides and their included angle, and ASA uses two angles and the included side. Equal-radius arcs construct perpendicular bisectors and angle bisectors; copied corresponding angles construct parallel lines.

Straightedge-and-compass construction keeps exact geometric conditions. The diagram shows an SSS construction: segment AB is drawn first, then an arc centred at A and an arc centred at B. The arcs meet at C above AB and at C′ below it, so there are two possible triangles, mirror images of each other in AB. Equal-radius arcs from the two ends of a segment locate points the same distance from both ends; joining two such points gives the perpendicular bisector.

Keep construction arcs visible because they are the evidence. For SSS, draw one side and intersect two circles. For SAS, construct the included angle between the two known sides. For ASA, construct the two known angles at the ends of the known side. Verify lengths and angles after construction.

sections.title: Worked example: decide whether a triangle can be constructed

prompt.text: Can a triangle be constructed with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 8 cm?

content.text: Draw the longest side, 8 cm. Then draw an arc of radius 3 cm from one end and an arc of radius 4 cm from the other end.
The arcs can reach at most 3 + 4 = 7 cm along the 8 cm side, so they never meet. There is no point for the third vertex.

sections.verification_note: Any two sides of a triangle must add to more than the third side. Here 3 + 4 is less than 8, so no triangle exists.

sections.title: Worked example: an SSS construction

prompt.text: Construct triangle ABC with AB = 7 cm, AC = 5 cm and BC = 8 cm, then explain why there are two possible positions for C.

content.text: With centre A and radius 5 cm, draw an arc. With centre B and radius 8 cm, draw a second arc.
Label an intersection C and join AC and BC. The arcs also meet at a second point C′ on the other side of AB, as in the diagram; triangle ABC′ is the mirror image of triangle ABC.

sections.verification_note: Check: 5 + 7 > 8, so the arcs do meet. Measure AC and BC, and keep both arcs visible as evidence of the construction.

blocks.text: Do not erase the arcs used to locate a point. A ruler with no compass construction does not demonstrate an exact bisector. Check that two arcs actually intersect; otherwise the proposed triangle data may be impossible.

prompt.text: A perpendicular bisector crosses a 12 cm segment. How far is the crossing from an endpoint?

feedback.text: The crossing is the midpoint, 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm.

blocks.text: SSS: draw one side, then intersect arcs from its ends. SAS: construct the included angle between the two sides. ASA: construct both angles at the ends of the given side. Equal-radius arcs from the ends of a segment give its perpendicular bisector.
Check that the data can make a figure (any two sides of a triangle must add to more than the third), keep every arc visible, and measure the finished figure.
